dedupe_keys.name: berec databases of public warning systems and means of access to emergency services in europe

description: BEREC, the body of European telecom regulators, maintains two Union-wide databases on emergency communications as part of its tools, built so that national operators, regulators and other competent authorities know which means are deployed in each country, including for roaming users. Coverage: EU and EEA member states plus Moldova and Ukraine; the Public Warning Systems database had 49 entries on 28 September 2026, giving country, type of system (cell broadcast, location-based SMS, app or other), links to the service and descriptions, for example BE-Alert in Belgium or BG-ALERT cell broadcast in Bulgaria; the Access to Emergency Services database had 94 entries listing emergency numbers and voice calls, emergency apps, messaging, relay services, real-time text and total conversation, with download links and notes. Format and access: filterable web tables with CSV export and a JSON view for each database, and e-mail subscriptions to updates; free and without registration. Licence: not stated on the pages read. Caveats: entries are reported by national authorities in free text, with uneven detail and some systems noted as under construction; the other BEREC tools (general authorisation, numbering and value added service databases) and BEREC's reports and roaming data were not recorded here. Simulation uses: which warning channels and emergency access means exist per country, for emergency response and population alerting models that depend on mobile networks. Related records: Germany's NINA warnings (data-bbk-nina-warnings-api) and the Common Alerting Protocol (data-oasis-common-alerting-protocol-cap) cover warning content, and the 2023 US nationwide alert test (case_study-us-nationwide-alert-test-2023) shows a system under test.
